title: Is "Annotated" preferred for Body Fields over default parameters?
body:
### First Check

- [X] I added a very descriptive title here.
- [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search.
- [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information.
- [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer.
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
# This is the code from the existing docs:
# https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/body-fields/

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = Field(
        default=None, title="The description of the item", max_length=300
    )
    price: float = Field(gt=0, description="The price must be greater than zero")
    tax: float | None = None
```


### Description

There appear to be two ways to define Fields (like Query) in FastAPI: using the annotated method or the default value:

https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/fields/#the-annotated-pattern
https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/query-params-str-validations/

```py

# Option 1
from typing import Annotated
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class Model(BaseModel):
    int_list: list[Annotated[int, Field(gt=0)]]


# Option 2
class Model(BaseModel):
    int_list: list[int] = Field(gt=0)
```

In the query docs, [it is recommended to use Option 1, the Annotated type](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/query-params-str-validations/#advantages-of-annotated), for various reasons. However, the Field docs don't mention this advantage at all, and both the default example and the "non-Annotated" variant use the same pattern of Option 2.

Is it preferable to use Annotated for Body Fields, just like it is recommended for Query parameters?

If so - should we update the Body Field documentation to reflect that?
If not - should we at least document both variations in the Body Field docs?

### Operating System

Linux, Windows, macOS

N/A - documentation question

### FastAPI Version

0.109.2

### Pydantic Version

2.6.1

### Python Version

3.10

### Additional Context

_No response_

answer.body:
> Is it preferable to use Annotated for Body Fields, just like it is recommended for Query parameters?

No, Pydantic supports the use Annotated Fields, but it doesn't claim that it is a recommended approach. (There are pros and cons, and developers are free to choose what works best for them)

> If so - should we update the Body Field documentation to reflect that?

I don't think so

> If not - should we at least document both variations in the Body Field docs?

I don't think so, this is rather about how to use Pydantic (and not the FastAPI). The best way to learn about Pydantic features is to consult the Pydantic documentation.

(imho)
